question: Surveys carried out by the vessel ‘Abeille Marengo’, belonging to the French group Meridiam, for the laying of cable as part of the Great Sea Interconnector (GSI) project within the Greek continental shelf and territorial waters, in an area under Greek jurisdiction, have evolved into a battleground for dangerous schemes harmful to the people.

Following Greece’s issuance of a NAVTEX notification in relation to the surveys, the Turkish State – despite having no jurisdiction as a coastal state – issued an counter-NAVTEX (6 November) and a further NAVTEX (10 November), claiming that it had granted consent for to a project in a maritime area under its own jurisdiction, invoking the invalid TurkishLibyan memorandum.

France, in consultation with the Greek Government, issued a note verbale to Türkiye, opening the doors for Türkiye to make unacceptable claims and assert jurisdiction over the Greek continental shelf as a coastal state, presenting a fait accompli. The Commission is asked: 1.
What does it make of the counter-NAVTEX and the further NAVTEX issued by Türkiye and challenging the sovereign rights of Greece, an EU Member State?

What does it make of the recent ‘progress report’, in which the EU considers Türkiye as a ‘strategic partner’, while the country is making unacceptable claims in the Aegean and Eastern Mediterranean and has been occupying territories of Cyprus, an EU Member State, for 52 years, refusing to recognise the Republic of Cyprus?

What does it make of the fact that Member States and EU groups are promoting projects, in the context of energy competition, which are demonstrably profit-driven, but which do not secure cheaper energy for the people of Greece and Cyprus and ordinary Europeans, but instead plunge them into energy poverty, burdening them with exorbitant electricity, heating and fuel costs?
